newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says moves being mulled to curb peso fall.
newsitem.headline: Manila says moves being mulled to curb peso fall.

text.p: Philippine central bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday the monetary authorities were considering measures to prevent any further fall in the peso.
But, in a local radio interview, he declined to give any details.
"We are looking at measures to enforce if the peso continues to fall," Singson said.
The peso hit a record low of 30.24 to the dollar during Monday's session amid persistent turmoil in the region's currency markets.
However, the central bank stayed out of the market, letting it seek its own level.

The Philippines was given something of a reprieve on Tuesday when torrential rains closed banks and put a stop to currency trading and halted the stock exchange, where shares had also fallen sharply on Monday.

The peso is now about 14 percent below its level prior to the July 11 de facto devaluation when the central bank, running out of currency reserves, was forced to give in to a wave of speculative attacks on its currency.
Singson declined to give details of the measures being considered, but said the policy-making Monetary Board met twice on Monday to discuss the measures.

The central bank has been tightening domestic liquidity to prevent banks using any excess pesos to buy dollars. Liquidity reserves of banks' deposits have been raised to five percent from two percent.
Singson also said the central bank was beefing up its dollar reserves, but again did not elaborate.

A local business newspaper reported that ING Bank has deposited $500 million with the central bank to help increase its international reserves. Both central bank and ING officials declined to confirm the report.
